title: SpaceInvite/get + SpaceBan/get return all account records, ignoring per-spec visibility scoping
description:
Sites:
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/invite.rs:20-58 (handle_invite_get)
- crate-jmap-chat-server/src/ban.rs:21-59 (handle_ban_get)

draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00:
- §SpaceInvite/get (line 1282-1284): 'Only members of the Space may retrieve its invites. Members with manage_members permission see all invites; other members see only invites they created.'
- §SpaceInvite/changes (line 1286-1288): same rules.
- §SpaceBan/get (line 1302-1304): 'Members with ban permission in the Space see all SpaceBan records for that Space. A banned user fetching their own account sees only SpaceBan records where userId matches their own identity.'

Both handlers do a plain backend.get_objects::<T>(caller, account_id, ids, None) and return the full list. The MemoryBackend's generic get_objects performs no visibility scoping. So any caller with JMAP access to the account sees every SpaceInvite or SpaceBan stored under that account, regardless of:
- which Space the invite/ban belongs to,
- whether the caller is a member of that Space,
- whether the caller holds manage_members / ban / is the invite owner / is the ban target.

Security impact:
- SpaceInvite codes are credentials. The handler leaks invite codes for any Space the caller doesn't otherwise have permission to access. A non-member can SpaceInvite/get a Space's invite list and use any of those codes to join.
- SpaceBan records leak the identities of banned users to non-privileged callers (and the ban reasons, which may be sensitive).

Fix: each /get handler post-filters the returned list per spec rules. Workspace backend-canonical policy says the backend should be the source of truth, but the kit can layer a defense-in-depth handler-side filter that calls backend.member_effective_permissions (a new sync-friendly read helper) and B::principal_id(caller) to project the allowed set.

For changes / queryChanges, the same filter must be applied to created/updated/destroyed id arrays — a caller who lost visibility to an invite/ban should not see its id in /changes either, otherwise the rate of new invites in a Space leaks.
close_reason: Landed on main as 8504fa21 (fix(chat-server): scope invite and ban reads). Adversarial review passed at the lane commit. Integration CI all green at 9e113188 (stable+beta 3448 passed).
